stories.title: Bitcoin's BIP-110 soft fork begins mandatory signaling with miner support under 3%
stories.summary: Bitcoin's contested BIP-110 proposal has moved into its mandatory signaling phase, with CoinDesk pegging the start around block 961,632. Cointelegraph reports miner support is currently below 3%, far short of the levels soft forks typically need to activate. Both outlets describe the proposal as controversial within the mining and developer community.
stories.whyItMatters: Soft forks change Bitcoin's consensus rules, and unusually low miner buy-in raises real doubt about whether this one activates — a concrete protocol-risk signal for anyone tracking Bitcoin's technical roadmap.
whatToWatch: Whether miner signaling support rises toward an activation threshold in the coming weeks
Reaction from major mining pools and core developers
What happens if the signaling window closes without sufficient support
questions: Why is miner support starting so low?
Is this fork attempt likely to be abandoned or retried?

stories.title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs post $1B week, best since April, with BlackRock taking 80% of inflows
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs together pulled in more than $1 billion over the week, their strongest showing since April, according to CryptoSlate. BlackRock's funds accounted for roughly 80% of that new money, underscoring how concentrated the inflow rebound has been among issuers.
stories.whyItMatters: A return of sizable ETF inflows — especially this concentrated in one issuer — is a concrete, trackable sign of institutional demand rather than sentiment alone.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows continue into next week
How flows split between Bitcoin and Ether funds
Whether other issuers start closing the gap with BlackRock
questions: What specifically drove this week's rebound?
Is BlackRock's outsized share reshaping ETF market structure long-term?

stories.title: Bitcoin, XRP, Solana and Tron have outpaced Ethereum and Cardano every month since 2022, CryptoSlate analysis finds
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate analysis of investor buying activity reportedly shows Bitcoin, XRP, Solana and Tron beating Ethereum and Cardano on a monthly basis in every month since 2022. The piece frames this as a multi-year pattern in where investor money has gone.
stories.whyItMatters: If accurate, a multi-year divergence in investor demand between these two groups of assets would matter for anyone weighing allocation among major chains beyond short-term price moves.
whatToWatch: Whether the pattern holds through coming months
Any follow-up detailing the underlying data or methodology
questions: What exactly is being measured — price, net inflows, or on-chain activity?
Does 'beating' account for market-cap differences between these assets?

stories.title: US spot Bitcoin ETFs post best week since April with $1B in inflows
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in roughly $1 billion over the past week, their strongest week since April, according to Cointelegraph. The report frames it as a notable pickup after a quieter stretch for the funds.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flow data is one of the cleaner real-time gauges of institutional Bitcoin demand, and a multi-month-high week is worth tracking regardless of daily price noise.

How this week's total compares once final daily figures are in

stories.title: Bitcoin's 'first institutional bear market' is starting to take shape, CryptoSlate reports
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports early signs of what it calls Bitcoin's first institutional bear market, marked by draining liquidity rather than the retail-driven selloffs of past cycles. The same outlet separately noted Bitcoin's ongoing AI-assisted security review flagged roughly 6,700 potential issues in 55 hours, though it's unclear how many represent genuine vulnerabilities.
stories.whyItMatters: A liquidity drain led by institutional rather than retail positioning would be a meaningfully different market dynamic than prior downturns, and is worth distinguishing from routine price volatility.
whatToWatch: Further liquidity and positioning data from CryptoSlate or other trackers
Any triage results narrowing the 6,700 flagged security issues down to confirmed ones
questions: What specifically defines this as an 'institutional' bear market versus prior ones?
How many of the flagged security issues turn out to be real?

stories.title: Senate to vote on advancing the CLARITY Act in September after Thune files cloture
stories.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune has filed cloture on the CLARITY Act, setting up a vote in September to advance the crypto market-structure bill, per Cointelegraph. The move is a procedural step toward getting the bill to the floor.
stories.whyItMatters: CLARITY Act is the central piece of US legislation meant to settle which regulator — the SEC or CFTC — oversees most crypto assets, making this vote a genuine milestone rather than routine political noise.
whatToWatch: The September cloture vote and whether it clears the 60-vote threshold
Any amendments attached before a floor vote
Industry and regulator reaction in the run-up
questions: Does the bill currently have the votes to pass?
What amendments might be added that change its substance?

stories.title: Brazil's central bank orders exchanges to delay large crypto transfers abroad
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank has ordered crypto exchanges operating in the country to delay large transfers of crypto assets abroad, according to CoinDesk. Specific thresholds and implementation timelines weren't detailed in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: A major emerging-market central bank imposing friction on crypto outflows is a concrete regulatory action that could affect liquidity and set a precedent other jurisdictions watch closely.
whatToWatch: What transfer size triggers the delay requirement
How exchanges implement compliance and by when
Whether other Latin American regulators follow suit
questions: What's driving the order — capital flight concerns, AML, something else?
How long is the mandated delay?

stories.title: Bitwise's Matt Hougan: 'trillions' in institutional money still to flow into bitcoin
stories.summary: Bitwise executive Matt Hougan says trillions of dollars in institutional capital have yet to flow into bitcoin, according to CoinDesk. The comments are framed as a forward-looking prediction rather than a report of actual flows.
stories.whyItMatters: Worth noting as a sentiment data point from a prominent crypto asset manager, but it's a forecast from someone whose firm sells bitcoin investment products — actual ETF flow figures are the better gauge of real institutional demand.
whatToWatch: Whether reported ETF and institutional flow data trends toward this thesis
Any specifics Hougan or Bitwise provide on timeline or sourcing for the claim
questions: What's the basis and timeframe behind the 'trillions' figure?
How does this square with the more modest weekly inflow numbers reported elsewhere?

stories.title: Nansen founder predicts bitcoin will never trade below $60,000 again

stories.whyItMatters: Price-floor predictions like this circulate widely and shape sentiment, but they reflect one person's view rather than confirmed market data — worth noting, not acting on.
whatToWatch: How bitcoin's price behaves relative to this claim over time
questions: What analysis, if any, underpins this specific price floor?
Has bitcoin traded near that level at any point this cycle?

stories.title: Bitcoin Lightning payment servers hit in latest infrastructure exploit
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports another exploit against Bitcoin infrastructure, this time draining Lightning Network payment servers. The report frames it as part of a pattern of recent infrastructure-level incidents rather than an isolated event.
stories.whyItMatters: Repeated exploits against Lightning infrastructure raise real operational-security concerns for a network that payment apps and merchants increasingly rely on for fast, low-cost bitcoin transactions.
whatToWatch: Which specific providers or servers were affected and how much was drained
Any funds recovery or compensation for affected users
Patches or hardening measures from Lightning implementations
questions: How much was actually drained, and from how many servers?
Is this connected to the broader wave of AI-discovered vulnerabilities being reported elsewhere?

stories.summary: According to a Hacker News-linked report, Danish high school students will be required to verbally defend their written assignments. No further detail on the policy's rationale, scope, or timeline was included in the supplied source.
stories.whyItMatters: This falls outside the crypto lane's usual focus on markets, protocols and regulation — it's included here only because it was among today's sourced items, and readers tracking digital-asset markets can safely skip it.
questions: What is driving this policy change, and when does it take effect?
